candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication adverse effects and teaching
candidate.educational_objective: Teach the client to promptly report unexplained muscle symptoms while taking atorvastatin.

options.A: Ignore the symptom unless it persists for several months.
options.B: Double the atorvastatin dose because muscle aching indicates inadequate lipid lowering.
options.C: Promptly report unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness, especially if accompanied by malaise or fever.
options.D: Stop all fluids until the muscle aching resolves.

candidate.rationale: Atorvastatin labeling instructs patients to promptly report unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness, particularly when accompanied by malaise or fever, because these may indicate clinically important myopathy.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Patients taking atorvastatin should promptly report unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness, particularly with malaise or fever.
candidate.source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine
candidate.stem: A client taking atorvastatin reports new unexplained muscle aching. Which teaching is most appropriate?
